title: Can you look like Toji Fushiguro in real life? (V-TAPER WORKOUT)
summary: He argues that Toji from Jujutsu Kaisen is a realistic physique goal and lists three mistakes common to anime workouts. He then lays out a three-stage, superset-based full-body program that focuses on shoulders, lats, traps, abs and neck, with minimal leg work, scaling from bodyweight work three days a week to a weighted four-day version.
claims: Unlike Yujiro Hanma, Toji's physique is a realistic goal
Mistake one: copying what the character does (e.g. swinging a sword to look like Guts) won't build the body; resistance training is the best way
Mistake two: matching a character's athletic feats doesn't give you his physique; doing 15 pull-ups won't give you the back of someone who can do 15 pull-ups
Mistake three: anime workouts are too frequent and too high-volume; most anime fans are novices with little work capacity, and you can't rush recovery
A good program should be relevant to the target look, scalable to experience and fun
Toji is an upper-body guy: dominant shoulders, lats and traps (the V-taper), standout abs, a thick neck, solid arms and chest, lagging forearms and smaller legs
Wide clavicles and narrow hips are genetic and can't be trained, but any training improves your V-taper, so don't dwell on it
Toji is about 6'2 (190 cm), probably over 200 lb, at 12-14% body fat; to get his abs you have to grow them rather than just get shredded, and staying moderately lean keeps the yoke and shoulders full
Stage 1 to stage 2 should take at least a year, and stage 2 to stage 3 at least two more; if you won't put in the time, give up now

Stage 1: full body on Monday, Wednesday and Friday as supersets of bodyweight compounds plus isolation (push-ups, chin-ups, laterals, shrugs, neck, abs, split squats); replace chin-ups with lat pulldowns if needed; experienced lifters can skip it
Upper back and long-head triceps get 4 sets because they are enduring; rear delts and forearms get fewer because untrained lifters fatigue them quickly
Pullovers are essential for the Toji V-taper; superset them with ab work because pullovers already stretch the abs
Upright rows stay at 10-15 reps so the weight stays low and you don't get hurt
Move to stage 2 once stage 1 no longer feels like enough volume: bodyweight moves become weighted, most exercises get harder variations, and most supersets gain a set
Weighted chin-ups stay at 6-10 reps; going too heavy tends to overextend the arm and risks a biceps injury
Stage 3 adds a Saturday session, about 30% more volume, and cuts one set from each Friday exercise so you stay fresh for Saturday
Farmers walks after pre-fatiguing traps, neck and shoulders are a killer trap builder
Shoulders, lats and traps are trained every session (3x a week, then 4x) while legs get little work, which makes the upper body look bigger by comparison
exercises: 3xAMRAP bodyweight, or lat pulldowns; superset with split squats 3x8-12
rear delts; lower sets since untrained
3x8-12 with a dumbbell, superset with Russian twists
traps and shoulders; higher reps to stay safe
4x4-8 (weighted push-ups allowed), superset with power shrugs 4x6-10
stage 2; power shrugs move more weight
stage 2 replaces reverse crunches to load the abs
replace dumbbell rows; hit traps harder
